holidays.name: National Unicorn Day
holidays.description: A day for glitter, rainbows and believing in magic. Fans of the mythical one-horned horse celebrate with sparkly outfits, unicorn crafts, and pastel treats.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on April calendars thanks to the creature's lasting appeal in folklore and pop culture.
holidays.funFact: The unicorn is the national animal of Scotland. It has appeared on Scottish royal coats of arms since the 1100s.

holidays.name: National Name Yourself Day
holidays.description: A day to ask what you would be called if you could choose. You might pick a bold new first name, a stage name, or a secret superhero alias, and try it out on friends for the day.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It invites people to play with identity and imagination.
holidays.funFact: Many famous people picked new names for themselves. Examples include Cary Grant, who was born Archibald Leach, and Elton John, who was born Reginald Dwight.

holidays.name: Cherish an Antique Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate old treasures, such as grandma's teapot, a creaky rocking chair, or a dusty pocket watch. It's a good excuse to dust off heirlooms, learn their stories, and visit an antique shop.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the history and craftsmanship in old objects.
holidays.funFact: Antiques are traditionally defined as items at least 100 years old. Items that are 20 to 99 years old are usually called vintage.
